description:
Umbrella for the three unfinished fast-follow epics left behind by shipped releases. Each child epic carries the findings its release deliberately did not take.

- specled_-scb — fast-follow of specled_-k6s (PR #32 / release 0.11.0 / main c2d21349). 4 children. NOTE: the dn4.12 and vbo branches are based on 2d4535c1, which is NOT an ancestor of squashed main — rebase with a cold worker before resuming.
- specled_-bg5 — fast-follow of specled_-q0q (PR #34 / release 0.13.0 / main 9adbac9c). 6 children from the 2026-08-06 critical review.
- specled_-vzd — fast-follow of specled_-n5q (PR #35 / release 0.14.0 / main bb64e69e). 6 children from the 2026-08-11 critical review.

Purpose: one place to see and sequence the accumulated post-release debt, so fast-follows get scheduled deliberately instead of aging out of `bw ready`. Suggested order is oldest-first (scb, then bg5, then vzd) since scb is the only one carrying rebase risk that grows with time.

No new work is defined here; this epic closes when all three child epics close.

Advances: specled.api_boundary, specled.realized_by

Operator decisions for this run:
- Scope: flattened — all 16 leaves across scb/bg5/vzd driven as one DAG under this epic.
- Decision-class tickets (vzd.1, bg5.1, vbo and any similar): the implementer drafts
  the decision + ADR as a proposal; the work is graded normally but is NOT merged.
  It waits for human sign-off at finish.

Tooling note: bin/rigor-check, pipeline-config, and gate-memo are NOT installed in this
repo/host. Consequences, applied for the whole run:
- No mechanical simple/critical authority, so every ticket is CRITICAL by the canonical
  rubric's default-when-unsure. No simple path; full grader ladder on every child.
- merge-batching is OFF, so merge gates run per-close.
- No gate memoization; every gate executes.

Known-red baselines: none (CLAUDE.md has no "Known Baseline Gate Exceptions" section).
Nothing is waivable this run.

CONTRACT SYNTHESIS COMPLETE — all 16 leaves. DAG below.

Three cold read-only analysts synthesized Advances / Allowed touches / Out of Scope (files) /
Out of Scope (intent) / Verification onto every leaf. Findings that changed the plan:

TICKET DEFECTS CORRECTED (the review findings were written as prose, not contracts):
- bg5.4 cited a "rejected" ADR status. No such status exists — the schema enum is
  ~w(accepted deprecated superseded) (lib/specled_ex/schema/decision.ex:5). Live exposure is
  deprecated + superseded. Re-chartered against those.
- bg5.5's premise was materially overstated. The :info COUNT is always printed with an explicit
  "info hidden; --verbose to show" disclosure (lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:252-257), spec'd
  since 0.8.0. Only the DETAIL line is hidden, and the flag is --verbose, not --debug.
- vzd.1's prescribed fix does not fix its stated defect: on a seeding run there is no committed
  entry, so no divergence finding exists for that MFA, so a per-MFA gate never fires. OPERATOR
  RE-CHARTERED to a run-scoped gate.
- vzd.3 shrinks by an order of magnitude: there is NO persisted append-only baseline to migrate
  (append_only.spec.md:9-11 — it is reconstructed per run), so no digest storage and no
  migration story. ~50 lines of detector; the cost is the budget justification.
- vzd.4's Advances was incomplete (1 subject listed, 3 actually spanned).
- vzd.6's Advances was wrong: specled.package is the distributed-artifact subject. OPERATOR
  MOVED it to specled.decisions as ADR-reference discipline.

HARD BLOCKER FOUND, PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED: specled_-bos had NO blocked_by edge, but
test/specled_ex/coverage/paths_test.exs — the only file it edits — does not exist at the epic
base. It is created by dn4.12. A worker dispatched on bos would have found nothing. Edge added.

DEPENDENCY EDGES ADDED THIS RUN:
  bg5.1 -> bg5.4 -> bg5.6      (all three must change authorizing_decision/2; bg5.1 settles the
                                authorization contract first)
  bg5.2 -> bg5.6
  vzd.4 -> vzd.2 -> vzd.1      (vzd.4 F13 renames drift_dangling_pairs/1, which vzd.2 reshapes)
  vzd.4 -> vzd.6               (vzd.4 deletes the very comment blocks vzd.6 would lint)
  dn4.12 -> bos                (NEW — hard blocker above)
  dn4.12 -> zd8                (pre-existing, re-verified against the actual diff)

ACCEPTED PRIORITY INVERSION: vzd.4 is P4 and vzd.2 is P3, but vzd.4 must land first. The
alternative is a guaranteed same-hunk conflict on the hot path.

OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED:
- vzd.1 -> re-charter to a run-scoped divergence gate (not the ticket's per-MFA gate).
- vzd.6 -> Advances: specled.decisions, not specled.package.
- vbo  -> drop Level C entirely, including its "deploy must not invoke mix" assertion; its
          helpers are the same run:-text-matching class that failed three times.

HELD FOR HUMAN SIGN-OFF (drafted and graded, but NOT merged): bg5.1, bg5.4, bg5.5, vzd.1,
vzd.3, vzd.6, vbo. Each needs a spec amendment or an ADR that changes what specled promises.

REBASE RESOLUTION (the two parked branches):
- dn4.12: a whole-branch rebase was the WRONG move — it replays 24 commits, 21 of which already
  landed in the 0.11.0 squash, manufacturing conflicts in package.spec.md and CLAUDE.md that
  belong to neither ticket. Correct operation is a cherry-pick of 2d4535c1..400839c3 (3 commits).
  DONE: clean, 6 files, +203/-113, .spec/realization_hashes.json untouched.
- vbo: merge-tree against the epic base is conflict-free in every class. Rebase then PRUNE
  rather than re-implement — ~150 lines both graders certified sound at iteration 3.

ORCHESTRATOR NOTE — contract/cadence conflict, resolved in favour of the cadence fence.

I wrote "mix test (FULL suite)" into specled_-vzd.4's Verification section, reasoning that a
four-part behavior-preservation claim deserves wide scope. That instruction is unsatisfiable by
a delegated implementer: the cadence block in delegated-implementer.md explicitly forbids a
per-ticket full-suite run and defers whole-system proof to the merge gate, and cx-implementer
BYTE-COMPARES that block against the canonical template before launching, so it cannot be
softened per-ticket even deliberately.

The implementer did the right thing — ran `mix test --stale` plus the three focused realization
files (98 tests) and left the full suite alone.

Resolution: the full-suite obligation for vzd.4 moves to this epic's per-close merge gate, which
runs it anyway. I briefed the verifier explicitly NOT to report the missing full-suite run as a
Gap, so it does not bounce a ticket for obeying its own template.

Standing correction for the rest of this run: a ticket contract's Verification section may ADD
targeted commands, but must never demand the full suite. If a ticket genuinely needs
whole-system proof, that is the merge gate's job and should be stated as a merge-gate note, not
an implementer instruction. No other contract in this epic carries a full-suite line; vzd.4 was
the only one.

LESSONS
- [other] On a re-chartered ticket, verify every grader record's provenance before letting it satisfy a gate — match Session tag AND graded commit against the current deliverable, never mere presence of the marker (from specled_-dn4.12)

Context for that line, because it nearly cost a false auto-approval:

specled_-dn4.12 carries 27 comments. SIX are TEST_CRITIC / AUDIT records from the earlier k6s
epic run (session b19669f0, 2026-07-27), including a `TEST_CRITIC: PASS` and an
`AUDIT: APPROVE (auto — selective audit)`. They grade commits bba184e2 and 5069e23e against a
0.11.0-era base. The current deliverable is c14f67f3 on bb64e69e.

A presence check — "does this ticket carry an elixir-test-critic record?" — returns TRUE on that
ticket and would have closed the Selective Audit Gate using a critic report for a different tree
in a different epic. The gate's own wording is what saved it: a record is a CONDITION TO BE MET,
and meeting it means a record that grades THIS diff.

Two tickets in this epic carry stale grader trails from prior runs: specled_-dn4.12 and
specled_-vbo. Both were re-chartered with fresh bounce budgets. When either reaches its gate,
read the LATEST comment via --json and confirm its Session tag is `i4x-*` and its graded commit
matches the stage tip. `bw-marker latest` reads only the newest comment and is safe; scanning the
body for a marker substring is not.

Action taken: dn4.12's stale critic records were rejected, the non-responsive critic was reaped,
and a fresh cold critic was spawned with an explicit instruction naming the stale records and
forbidding reuse of their conclusions.

LESSONS
- [other] On a re-chartered ticket, verify every grader record's provenance before letting it satisfy a gate — match Session tag AND graded commit against the current deliverable, never mere presence of the marker (from specled_-dn4.12)
- [unwired-call-path] When a refactor widens a shared helper's callback contract, update every caller of that helper, not only the callers the test suite reaches — enumerate call sites mechanically before claiming zero behavior change (from specled_-vzd.4)
- [untested-clause] Never broaden a source-scanning guard assertion to accommodate a new sibling function; keep the form that requires a real call site, or the guard starts matching prose (from specled_-bg5.2)

Both of this round's verification failures share a shape worth naming: THE REPO'S OWN GATES
CANNOT SEE EITHER DEFECT.

specled_-vzd.4 — F9 widened dedupe_by_mfa/2's callback from "return {:ok, raw_hash_binary}" to
"return {:ok, entry}". The three compute_tier_hashes/3 clauses were updated; the three
compute_seed_hashes/3 clauses (orchestrator.ex:760, :769, :778) were not. The seed path now
writes raw SHA-256 bytes where an entry map belongs and HashStore.merge/2 dies with
FunctionClauseError on the default gate path. Every contract gate passed anyway — this repo
declares ZERO expanded_behavior/typespecs/use bindings, and the single multi-tier orchestrator
test runs umbrella?: true + commit_hashes?: false, so it skips seeding. The FULL SUITE WOULD NOT
CATCH IT EITHER. The verifier proved it by running Orchestrator.run both ways and isolating the
regression to orchestrator.ex alone.

specled_-bg5.2 — the anti-hardcoding guard at severity_integration_test.exs:204 was weakened from
`Severity.resolve(` to `Severity.resolve`. The shorter substring is satisfied by a DOC COMMENT at
branch_check.ex:352. The verifier built a branch_check.ex with all three resolver call sites
renamed away, comment intact, and showed the new assertion still passes while the old one fires.
The two sibling `refute` assertions in that test were already vacuous, so this was the only live
guard — the test's own docstring is now false.

Neither would have been caught by a green suite, a green spec.check, or a green merge gate. Both
were caught only because a cold verifier was told to falsify the ticket's central claim rather
than confirm it. That is the argument for keeping first-verify at high-class on every ticket in
this epic, including the ones that look mechanical.

CROSS-BRANCH INTERACTION — recorded now so it is not discovered at merge time.

specled_-bg5.6 and specled_-vzd.3 both change how the append_only finding-code catalog is derived,
on SEPARATE branches, and neither can see the other:

- vzd.3 ADDS a code (append_only/statement_rewritten) to lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex, registers it
  in branch_check.ex @per_code_defaults, and updates the hand-maintained @append_only_codes mirror
  in test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs.
- bg5.6 REPLACES the regex source-scan in test/test_support/emitter_codes.ex with a
  @doc false SpecLedEx.AppendOnly.finding_codes/0 export, and repoints three catalogs at it —
  including that same docs-lint mirror.

The mirror-drift test asserts set equality in BOTH directions between the hand-maintained list and
the codes extracted from lib source. So whichever of these merges SECOND will need its extraction
and its mirror reconciled against the other's change. This is not a conflict either worker can
resolve from its own branch, and I deliberately told bg5.6 NOT to hardcode or future-proof for
vzd.3's code — inventing a placeholder for work on another branch is how a catalog silently goes
wrong.

Both tickets are HELD, so the operator sees both before either lands. Sequencing note for the
sign-off session: land bg5.6 FIRST (it changes the derivation mechanism), then vzd.3 (which adds a
code through that mechanism). The reverse order works too but forces vzd.3's mirror edit to be
redone against a derivation that no longer exists.

Neither ticket is defective. This is a genuine parallelism cost of running the two lineages
concurrently, and it is cheap to pay at sign-off with both diffs in hand.

LESSONS
- [other] On a re-chartered ticket, verify every grader record's provenance before letting it satisfy a gate — match Session tag AND graded commit against the current deliverable, never mere presence of the marker (from specled_-dn4.12)
- [unwired-call-path] When a refactor widens a shared helper's callback contract, update every caller of that helper, not only the callers the test suite reaches — enumerate call sites mechanically before claiming zero behavior change (from specled_-vzd.4)
- [untested-clause] Never broaden a source-scanning guard assertion to accommodate a new sibling function; keep the form that requires a real call site, or the guard starts matching prose (from specled_-bg5.2)
- [other] Never copy an analyst's factual claim into a ticket contract as authoritative without verifying it first — a wrong premise in a contract propagates into shipped code and false comments (from specled_-dn4.12 and specled_-vzd.6)
- [other] When a contract directs replacing one side of a two-sided mirror, state the invariant that makes it safe — both sides must derive from DIFFERENT mechanisms — or the substitution reads as permission to unify them (from specled_-bg5.6)

ORCHESTRATOR SELF-ASSESSMENT — the contract failed twice, in the same way.

Two defects this epic trace to factual claims I wrote into contracts without checking:

1. specled_-dn4.12: I wrote that lib/specled_ex/coverage/arming.ex is "NOT on any spec surface: list"
   and offered it as the precedent for keeping paths.ex off one. arming.ex IS on
   coverage_capture's surface list (.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:94). The directive was still
   correct and the gate agreed, so nothing shipped wrong — but the justification was false.

2. specled_-vzd.6: I wrote that orchestrator.ex:216-248 "restates no ADR" and listed it as a block
   that CANNOT honestly carry a pointer. specled.decision.file_touch_yields_to_realization governs
   that function directly and the block restates its Decision section nearly clause for clause. Here
   the false premise DID ship into the deliverable: the implementer wrote an exemption marker
   asserting "no governing ADR", converting a missing-pointer defect into an asserted-absence one —
   the exact class the ticket exists to eliminate.

Common cause: I treated the contract-synthesis analysts' measurements as verified because they were
detailed and cited line numbers. Detail is not verification. Both claims were single greps away from
being checked and I checked neither.

A third, different failure: on specled_-bg5.6 my SCOPE ADDITION was not false but UNDER-SPECIFIED —
it named a substitution without stating the invariant that made it safe, and the implementer
reasonably read it as permission to unify both sides of a drift mirror. The audit corrected my
over-correction there too: my first instinct was to withdraw the instruction entirely, which would
have discarded sound work to fix a problem I had misdiagnosed.

What caught all three: cold verification with an explicit instruction to falsify rather than confirm.
No gate, no suite, and no amount of contract detail would have found them. That is the argument for
keeping first-verify high-class on every ticket in this epic, including the ones that looked
mechanical — three of the four wave-1 tickets that "looked simple" carried real defects.

TOOLING TRAP — recorded because I have been actively causing it in this epic's contracts.

`mix test --only spec:<id>` SILENTLY SELECTS NOTHING for any multi-element list `@tag spec:` value
in this repo. Single-element lists and plain strings match fine; a 2-element list does not. Found by
the specled_-vzd.1 verifier, which then proved the binding was nonetheless real via negative control
— renaming the tag to a bogus id makes `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` emit

  [WARNING] specled.realized_by tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag ... covers
  specled.realized_by.silent_seed_run_scoped_divergence_gate but no test carries @tag spec: ...

and it does NOT fire on the real tree. So the tag scan is live and sees the list tag; only the
`--only` CLI selector is blind to it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TICKET: I have repeatedly written "prove it by tag — run
`mix test --only spec:<id>`" into ticket contracts and verifier briefs this epic. Against a
multi-element list tag that command reports `0 tests` and exits 1, which reads exactly like a broken
or unflipped stub. A less careful verifier would report a Gap that does not exist, or an implementer
would "fix" a working tag. specled_-vzd.2's own 2-element tag is equally unselectable.

It does not affect specled's own verification, which runs a MERGED full `mix test` and attributes
per-cover by static tag scan — so nothing shipped is wrong. It is a trap for humans and agents
reading the CLI.

Not filed as a ticket: it is internal-tooling ergonomics, and this epic exists to CLOSE a backlog.
Surfaced to the operator instead. If the "prove it by tag" instruction is going to keep being issued
in contracts — and it should, it caught real things here — then either the selector should match
list tags or the instruction should say to run the file and grep, not `--only`.

MINI-RETRO

WHERE THE BOUNCES CAME FROM, since the split matters more than the total:
- vzd.4 — implementer defect. A refactor widened a shared helper's callback contract and updated 3
  of 6 call sites; the seed path then wrote raw hash bytes and HashStore.merge/2 crashed on the

- bg5.1 — implementer defect, test-net only. Production was correct; the fixture ids happened to

- bg5.3 — implementer defect. A security doc named only one of the two tasks that execute
  repo-authored shell by default, filing the other on the safe side.
- bg5.6 — SHARED. My SCOPE ADDITION named a substitution without stating the invariant that made it

- vzd.6 — SHARED, mostly mine. My contract asserted as measurement that a comment block "restates no
  ADR". It was false, and the implementer shipped an exemption marker on that premise — converting a
  missing-pointer defect into an asserted-absence one.

TWO OF FIVE BOUNCES TRACE TO FALSE FACTUAL CLAIMS I WROTE INTO CONTRACTS. Both had the same cause:
I copied contract-synthesis analysts' measurements into authoritative-sounding contract lines because
they were detailed and cited line numbers. Detail is not verification. The durable fix is the lesson
already recorded: contract measurements about ADR coverage or surface membership must cite the
command that produced them.

WHAT THE PIPELINE CAUGHT THAT NO GATE COULD:
- 3 of the 4 wave-1 tickets that "looked mechanical" carried real defects.
- vzd.4's crash would have shipped: enabled_tiers defaults to nil and falls back to all four tiers,
  so no adopter opt-in was needed. The repo's own suite and full suite are both blind to it.
- bg5.6's freeze bug dropped codes added through the SANCTIONED constructor, purely by source
  position.
- A stale TEST_CRITIC: PASS and AUDIT: APPROVE from the k6s epic sat on dn4.12 grading different
  commits on a 0.11.0-era base. A presence check on the marker would have closed that gate on the
  wrong evidence.

ONE ORCHESTRATION ERROR OF MY OWN, beyond the contracts: I rendered specled_-vzd.6's prompt, labelled
it phase:implementing, and never invoked the launcher. It sat ~45 minutes with no worker. The label
and the provisioned run directory both made it look live. My checks confirm shape, not substance —
the same class as the prompt-validator passing a bounce prompt whose audit block had been silently
emptied by shell quoting.

A cleanup note worth recording, because it cost two wrong attempts: `make worktree-cleanup` takes
NAME as the FULL directory basename (specled_ex-trailer-provenance, not trailer-provenance), and
WORKTREE_CLEANUP_BASE must be set to the EPIC BRANCH when removing stages merged into an epic rather
than into main. Run from the main checkout — running from the epic worktree makes the target derive
paths from the wrong project prefix. With the default base (HEAD=main) every stage correctly refused,
since none of this work is on main yet. That refusal was the gate doing its job, not an obstacle.

The epic remains OPEN and in progress. The branch is NOT pushed and no PR is opened — that is the
human checkpoint.

16 of 16 merged. Epic branch 27 commits over main, 51 files, 7 ADRs, 1365 tests, 455 requirements
across 34 subjects. Final gate: validate errors=0 warnings=0; spec.check result=pass.

THE THREE MERGE-PHASE BOUNCES were all cross-ticket collisions that only became visible because the
merge order was chosen deliberately rather than alphabetically:

- specled_-bg5.6 — rebasing would have SILENTLY DELETED specled_-vzd.5's merged full-set-claim
  requirement, because bg5.6 was cut before vzd.5 landed and both rewrote the same must. Neither
  side conflicts semantically; git simply cannot merge two rewrites of one paragraph.
- specled_-vzd.3 — its new emitter was a PLAIN MAP where bg5.6's catalog only sees macro-registered
  codes. A flawless textual merge would have shipped a ticket whose fourteenth code, budgeted with
  an entire supersedes ADR, never reached the catalog. Caught by asking the rebase worker to report
  which FORM the emitter took.
- specled_-vzd.6 — its own corrected comment went STALE between its bounce fix and its merge, when
  vzd.1 changed the function that comment describes. The ticket that exists to stop comment drift
  had its remediation comment drift.

None of the three would have been caught by a green suite. All three were caught because rebase
workers were forbidden to hand-resolve and required to report hunk headers.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, beyond the two contract errors already recorded:
- I ran a rebase in parallel with another ticket's merge, which invalidated it and cost a redo.
  Every merge invalidates every pending rebase; per-close gates make that structural.
- I computed branch diffs against stale bases twice, and a shell redirect silently reused a
  previous file under noclobber, producing a confidently wrong overlap report. Both are the same
  shape as the defects this epic kept finding: a check that looks like it ran and did not.
- I ran the first worktree cleanup from the main checkout, so WORKTREE_CLEANUP_BASE resolved to
  main and every stage correctly refused. The refusal was the gate working.

WHAT THE PIPELINE CAUGHT that no gate could: a crash that would have reached adopters on the
default path (vzd.4), a mirror comparing a set against itself (bg5.6), an attribute freeze that
silently dropped codes added through the sanctioned constructor (bg5.6), a security doc naming one
of two shell-executing tasks (bg5.3), a test whose fixture ids made its killing mutant invisible
(bg5.1), and a prescribed fix that provably did not fix its own defect (vzd.1).

human checkpoint.
